question.text: Under Regulation 20(11) of the SEBI (AIF) Regulations, appointing a custodian is mandatory for:

answer.text: Only Cat III AIFs exceeding INR 1,000 crore corpus.
Only AIFs with foreign investor participation.

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Chapter 9.7.2 states: 'Under the existing SEBI regulations, appointing a custodian is mandatory for all AIFs. Each scheme can have a different custodian however in order to segregate assets and liabilities.' Regulation 20(11) explicitly lists custodian duties including safekeeping and (for Cat III) physical commodity derivatives settlement. **The Trap:** Option A invents a corpus threshold. Option C limits it to open-ended; not correct. Option D limits it to FPIs; not correct. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C tests the custodian-mandate across tracks. XIX-D tests the same for Cat I/II with pre-2022 grandfathering. XXI-B (Portfolio Manager) also requires custodian for PMS above INR 500 crore; different threshold. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Segregate CUSTODIAN per scheme when your long-short scheme uses different prime brokers — custodian-level segregation aligns with the Custodian Agreement's responsibility fixation under Chapter 9.7.2.
